items_missed: Set Agenda: never asked 'how are you today,' and never gave a real agenda statement (what we'll cover + rough time + 'sound good?') before diving into questions.

Probe: no origin zip code, no ask about garage/storage/additional rooms, no special-considerations question (narrow hallways, tight turns), never asked if she needs packing help, no storage or additional-stop questions, and no parking/HOA check.
Pricing: skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener, and never mentioned the Meet Your Mover email at all.

Estimate: didn't tie the origin's stairs/elevator access into the time estimate, no walk-distance discussion, no equivalents/comparisons used to make the hours tangible, and never stated a truck count.
Save Your Ass: the entire prep speech was skipped - no prep-ahead framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip - even though the customer directly asked how to bring the cost down.

Quote/Booking: no attempt to lock in the date on the call, no deposit-required mention, nothing said about the bolded detail list at the top of the email, no 'reply with any corrections,' no 'any other questions before I let you go,' and no hours/contact info given.
Politeness: never used the customer's name (Rafiq) a single time on the call.
Bonus: no rapport-building or humor moment, and missed the budget-conscious framing opportunity right when the customer asked about a split move to save money.
top_strength: The insurance explanation was genuinely strong and specific - Lukas contrasted the No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000 per move) against the 60 cent/lb baseline with a concrete example ('a 50 lb TV gets knocked over... with the state coverage they'll give you like $30'), which makes the value obvious to a customer who's never heard the distinction before.
coaching_note: The biggest miss here is skipping Save Your Ass completely - the customer literally asked 'do you offer anything to reduce the cost,' which is the exact opening that speech is built for, and Lukas answered with just 'no' on split moves instead. Also work in the customer's name a few times (never used 'Rafiq' once) and give a real agenda statement up front instead of jumping straight into move questions. Pricing math itself was accurate and clearly explained, but slow down - the pricing paragraph runs on for a long stretch without a breath, and you called yourself out for talking fast because of caffeine, which is a sign to pace it deliberately rather than push through.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and cooperative throughout with one light self-deprecating moment (the caffeine comment), but long run-on sentences and zero use of the customer's name keep it from feeling like real rapport rather than a transactional walk-through.
